articles.standfirst: Bosses of Citroën owner and French carmaker also urge UK government to consider limiting imports from China

gist: Stellantis and Renault want the UK included in upcoming EU protection rules.
Executives suggested the British government should think about limiting Chinese car imports.
The EU plans to restrict certain vehicle imports from China to protect local manufacturing.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Stellantis and Renault bosses supported including the UK in proposed EU measures meant to shield local vehicle production. Speaking in Paris, they argued that Britain ought to be treated like an EU member state under the upcoming Industrial Accelerator Act, provided the UK addresses concerns regarding Chinese vehicle imports.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: European automotive makers face intense pressure from lower demand and soaring Chinese market share. Including the UK could safeguard cross-border manufacturing footprints, but disagreements remain over whether Britain should restrict Chinese imports similarly to the EU.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The EU intends to enforce a quota on Chinese hybrid vehicle imports starting in December. Meanwhile, the UK government is reviewing its stance on whether to impose its own tariffs on Chinese vehicle imports.

gist: John Branfield died aged 95, leaving a legacy as a teacher and novelist.

He is survived by four children, two grandchildren and a sister.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: English teacher and novelist John Branfield has died aged 95. Born in Somerset, he studied at Cambridge, taught in France and Middlesex, and later settled in Cornwall where he taught at Camborne County grammar school for girls until 1980. Alongside teaching, he wrote novels for adults and teenagers, later shifting to books about the Newlyn school of painters.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Branfield built a wider audience with teenage novels such as The Fox in Winter, which was runner-up for the Carnegie Medal for Writing. He and his late wife Pep also built an impressive collection of Cornish art and ceramics, which they loaned to local galleries and co-curated into exhibitions.
